# WSL

Work in WSL (Windows Subsystem for Linux) across the Windows and Linux boundary. The
wsl.exe management and interop commands are in
[references/commands.md](references/commands.md).

## Rules

- **Keep project files on the Linux filesystem (`~/...`), not under `/mnt/c/...`.** Access
  through `/mnt` is much slower, and its case and permission rules differ.
- **Run `command -v <tool>` when a tool behaves strangely.** Interop puts Windows
  executables on the Linux `PATH`, so `git`, `node` or `python` can resolve to a `.exe`.
- **Use the Linux toolchain for repository work.** Call `<tool>.exe` only when you want
  the Windows program, for example `explorer.exe .`.
- **Set `PATH` in the script, or run it through `bash -lc '...'`.** A non-interactive
  shell does not read your profile.
- **Keep LF line endings.** A Windows editor that writes CRLF breaks shell scripts and git
  hooks.

## Non-interactive and login shells

A login or interactive shell reads `~/.bashrc` or `~/.zshrc`. That profile loads version
managers and sets `PATH`. A script, a background job or a hook that an agent starts is
non-interactive and does not read the profile. So the `PATH`, the aliases and the version
managers of your terminal are not there. A command that works when you type it can then
fail from a script.

The node and nvm form of this problem is in the `node` skill.
